items.title: Lew Tabackin interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 17, 1999
items.q: big band work in New York with Larry Elgart, Maynard Ferguson, Buddy Morrow and others.

ctx.x: Lew Tabackin was born in Philadelphia on March 26, 1940. He played flute and tenor sax in public school and obtained a B.M. from the Philadelphia Conservatory of Music in 1962. After military service he began playing small group jazz with Tal Farlow and big band work in New York with Larry Elgart, Maynard Ferguson, Buddy Morrow and others. Lew has played with Elvin Jones, Roland Hanna, Donald Byrd and with a number of television studio bands. He is the featured soloist with the Toshiko Akiyoshi Jazz Orchestra and…
Lew was interviewed in New York City on January 17, 1999, by Monk Rowe, Director of the Fillius Jazz Archive.
